function.name: edit
function.description: Edit the contents of a file by finding and replacing exact text. When editing text from Read output, preserve the exact indentation (tabs or spaces) and omit the line-number prefix, such as `1: `. Never include the prefix in oldString or newString. Write line breaks as \n; the file's existing CRLF or LF line endings are matched and preserved. To change line endings themselves, make oldString and newString differ only in \r; that edit applies to the exact bytes. If there is no exact match, the edit retries while ignoring typographic quote, dash, and space variants, then trailing whitespace on each line. The edit fails if oldString is not found. By default, oldString must identify a UNIQUE location. Multiple matches FAIL unless replaceAll is true. Add more surrounding context to disambiguate, or set replaceAll to true to replace every occurrence. Use replaceAll when the change should apply to every occurrence, such as renaming a variable.

oldString.description: Exact text to find and replace

newString.description: Text to replace oldString with (must differ from oldString)

replaceAll.description: Whether to replace every occurrence of oldString. When false, oldString must match exactly once. Defaults to false.

function.name: experimental_image_generate
function.description:
Generates a new image, or edits existing ones.
Only call this when the user asks you to create or edit an image. If you think an image would help but the user didn't ask for one, ask them first instead of generating it.
Images you pass are used as the source to edit, or as references for style and subject.
Each call makes one image. For several images, call it once per image.
It runs in the background: the call starts a job and returns right away, and you are notified automatically when the image is saved, with its path. Never poll, sleep, or check for the file while you wait.
Don't repeat a request unless the user asks.

prompt.description: What to create, or for edits, what to change. Be specific about subject, style, composition and any text that should appear in the image.

images.description: Images to edit, or to use as references for style and subject when creating a new image, in order. Local file paths (relative to the session directory or absolute) or http(s) URLs.

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular image model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look it up with the models tool using type: "image", filtering to your own provider first.

path.description: Where to save the image, relative to the session directory or absolute. The extension is replaced with the image's real format, and an existing file is overwritten. Defaults to a new file in the session's temp folder.

function.name: glob
function.description: Search file paths using a glob pattern (examples: "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx").

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files against

path.description: Directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

hidden.description: Include hidden files and directories (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching files to return (default: 100)

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents using ripgrep's regular expression syntax or literal text matching. Use it to locate specific code, symbols, or text patterns, and narrow searches with `path` or `include`. Returns matching file paths, line numbers, and line previews.

pattern.description: Regular expression or literal text to match in file contents.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: Glob pattern to filter files (for example, "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}")

literal.description: Treat `pattern` as exact text instead of a regular expression (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default: 100)

function.name: playwright_browser_click
function.description: Perform click on a web page

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

doubleClick.description: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click

button.description: Button to click, defaults to left

function.name: playwright_browser_close
function.description: Close the page

function.name: playwright_browser_console_messages
function.description: Returns all console messages

level.description: Level of the console messages to return. Each level includes the messages of more severe levels. Defaults to "info".

all.description: Return all console messages since the beginning of the session, not just since the last navigation. Defaults to false.

filename.description: Filename to save the console messages to. If not provided, messages are returned as text.

function.name: playwright_browser_drag
function.description: Perform drag and drop between two elements

startElement.description: Human-readable source element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

startTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

endElement.description: Human-readable target element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

endTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.name: playwright_browser_drop
function.description: Drop files or MIME-typed data onto an element, as if dragged from outside the page. At least one of "paths" or "data" must be provided.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

paths.description: Absolute paths to files to drop onto the element.

data.description: Data to drop, as a map of MIME type to string value (e.g. {"text/plain": "hello", "text/uri-list": "https://example.com"}).

function.name: playwright_browser_evaluate
function.description: Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.description: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided

filename.description: Filename to save the result to. If not provided, result is returned as text.

function.name: playwright_browser_file_upload
function.description: Upload one or multiple files

paths.description: The absolute paths to the files to upload. Can be single file or multiple files. If omitted, file chooser is cancelled.

function.name: playwright_browser_fill_form
function.description: Fill multiple form fields

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

value.description: Value to fill in the field. If the field is a checkbox, the value should be `true` or `false`. If the field is a combobox, the value should be the text of the option.

function.name: playwright_browser_find
function.description: Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page for text or a regular expression. Returns matching snapshot nodes with a few lines of surrounding context (like search snippets), each shown under its path from the root of the tree, which is cheaper than capturing the whole snapshot when you only need to locate an element and its ref.

text.description: Plain text to search for in the page snapshot (case-insensitive substring match). Provide either text or regex, not both.

regex.description: Regular expression to search for in the page snapshot. Matching is case-sensitive by default; wrap the pattern in slashes to add flags, e.g. "/error/i" for case-insensitive. Provide either text or regex, not both.

function.name: playwright_browser_handle_dialog
function.description: Handle a dialog

promptText.description: The text of the prompt in case of a prompt dialog.

function.name: playwright_browser_hover
function.description: Hover over element on page

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.name: playwright_browser_navigate
function.description: Navigate to a URL

function.name: playwright_browser_navigate_back
function.description: Go back to the previous page in the history

function.name: playwright_browser_network_request
function.description: Returns full details (headers and body) of a single network request, or a single part if `part` is set. Use the number from browser_network_requests.

index.description: 1-based index of the request, as printed by browser_network_requests.

part.description: Return only this part of the request. Omit to return full details.

filename.description: Filename to save the result to. If not provided, output is returned as text.

function.name: playwright_browser_network_requests
function.description: Returns a numbered list of network requests since loading the page. Use browser_network_request with the number to get full details.

static.description: Whether to include successful static resources like images, fonts, scripts, etc. Defaults to false.

filter.description: Only return requests whose URL matches this regexp (e.g. "/api/.*user").

filename.description: Filename to save the network requests to. If not provided, requests are returned as text.

function.name: playwright_browser_press_key
function.description: Press a key on the keyboard

function.name: playwright_browser_resize
function.description: Resize the browser window

function.name: playwright_browser_run_code_unsafe
function.description: Run a Playwright code snippet. Unsafe: executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright server process and is RCE-equivalent.

code.description: A JavaScript function containing Playwright code to execute. It will be invoked with a single argument, page, which you can use for any page interaction. For example: `async (page) => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click(); return await page.title(); }`

filename.description: Load code from the specified file. If both code and filename are provided, code will be ignored.

function.name: playwright_browser_select_option
function.description: Select an option in a dropdown

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

values.description: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

function.name: playwright_browser_snapshot
function.description: Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page, this is better than screenshot

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

filename.description: Save snapshot to markdown file instead of returning it in the response.

depth.description: Limit the depth of the snapshot tree

boxes.description: Include each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height] in the snapshot. Coordinates are viewport-relative, in CSS pixels (Element.getBoundingClientRect)

function.name: playwright_browser_tabs
function.description: List, create, close, or select a browser tab.

index.description: Tab index, used for close/select. If omitted for close, current tab is closed.

url.description: URL to navigate to in the new tab, used for new.

function.name: playwright_browser_take_screenshot
function.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. You can't perform actions based on the screenshot, use browser_snapshot for actions.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

type.description: Image format for the screenshot. Default is png.

filename.description: File name to save the screenshot to. Defaults to `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg}` if not specified. Prefer relative file names to stay within the output directory.

fullPage.description: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

scale.description: Image resolution scale. "css" produces a screenshot sized in CSS pixels (smaller, consistent across devices). "device" produces a high-resolution screenshot using device pixels (larger, accounts for the device pixel ratio). Default is css.

function.name: playwright_browser_type
function.description: Type text into editable element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

text.description: Text to type into the element

submit.description: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)

slowly.description: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

function.name: playwright_browser_wait_for
function.description: Wait for text to appear or disappear or a specified time to pass

textGone.description: The text to wait for to disappear

function.name: question
function.description:
Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution. This allows you to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take.

Usage notes:
- A "Type your own answer" option is added automatically; don't include a separate option for free form answers
- Set `multiple: true` to allow selecting more than one option
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

function.name: railway-machine_bootstrap_get
function.description: Inspect one agent bootstrap by id: its status and the manifest its active version reported. Stored variables are injected into the process env of machines booted from it and are not shown here.

function.name: railway-machine_bootstrap_list
function.description: List the agent bootstraps in this Railway environment: id, name, status, and when each was last saved. The one this machine was booted from, if any, is marked.

function.name: railway-machine_bootstrap_save
function.description: Save this machine as a version of an agent bootstrap: a snapshot of its disk that future agents in this Railway environment boot from warm, with repos, dependencies, caches, and the files under /etc/railway/bootstrap intact. Pass `name` to create a new bootstrap, or `id` (from bootstrap_list) to save a new version onto an existing one, optionally renaming it with `name`. This machine was not booted from a bootstrap, so `id` or `name` is required. Use it when the user asks to save, snapshot, or update a bootstrap, or wants future agents to start already set up. Recommended before saving, outside /app (the user's code): /etc/railway/bootstrap/startup.sh, bash that runs on every boot and wake of machines created from the bootstrap (keep it idempotent and non-blocking; output lands in /etc/railway/bootstrap/logs/startup.log), and /etc/railway/bootstrap/AGENTS.md, notes future sessions read. `variables` merge into the bootstrap's stored variables and are injected into the process env of every machine booted from it: a string sets a key, `null` removes it, and values may reference other Railway variables with ${{...}}. Ask the user in chat for secret values; never write them to disk. Pass `capture: false` to change only variables or the name while keeping the current snapshot. A capture runs in the background and does not disturb this session.

name.description: Bootstrap name, e.g. "dev". Creates a new bootstrap without `id`; with `id`, renames it.

variables.description: Environment variables to merge; `null` removes a key.

capture.description: Snapshot the disk as a new version (default true). false keeps the current snapshot and only applies `variables` and `name`; needs `id`, or this machine's own bootstrap when both `id` and `name` are omitted.

function.name: railway-machine_ship
function.description: Deploy the app in the working directory to a Railway service and return its public URL. Use this whenever the user asks to ship, deploy, publish, or put the app in production. The first ship creates the target service and records it; later ships redeploy the same service automatically. This never deploys to the machine's own service. The deploy runs through the build and can take several minutes; pass detach: true to return as soon as the upload is accepted.

name.description: Service name when the first ship creates the target service. Pick a short kebab-case name from the app's own context — its package, repo, or product name (e.g. "pixel-editor", "acme-api"). Defaults to "web". Ignored once a target is recorded.

serviceId.description: Deploy to this exact existing Railway service id and record it as the target. Only pass when the user explicitly names a service to deploy to; otherwise omit.

detach.description: Start the deploy and return once the upload is accepted instead of waiting for the build. Defaults to false.

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

function.name: shell
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Commands run on Linux using bash. Quote file paths containing spaces or special characters. Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

function.name: skill
function.description:
Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
Subagents always run in the background: the call returns immediately with a sessionID, and you receive a `<subagent>` message each time the child goes idle, including after later work.
Keep working on non-overlapping tasks, or briefly tell the user what you launched and end your response. Do not sleep, poll, or proactively check on the child's progress.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Pass the returned sessionID to continue that specific child conversation. A follow-up to a running child joins its current run.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. It must be a chat model; image and decision models can't run subagents. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Send a follow-up to an existing subagent, running or finished. Omit to start a new one.

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
Fetch content from an HTTP or HTTPS URL and return it as text, markdown, or HTML. Markdown is the default.

Use a more targeted tool when one is available. This tool is read-only. Large text results may be replaced with a preview while the complete output is retained in managed storage.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

function.name: websearch
function.description:
Search the web using the user's selected search integration. Use this for current information beyond knowledge cutoff.

The current year is 2026. Use this year when searching for recent information or current events.

function.name: write
function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

Missing parent directories are created automatically.

Use this tool to create new files or overwrite existing files. For partial changes, use the edit tool instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write to

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
Write plain JavaScript and send it exactly as written: no code fence, and no JSON or other wrapper around it.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable: there is no `setTimeout` or sleep. All other external access goes through `tools`.
Inside `execute`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.
